subject: HelixPay: cost sensitivity & next-step checklist (post-discovery)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@helixpay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: HelixPay discovery — cost sensitivity & next-step checklist

Hi Ravi —

Thanks again for the 30-min call today. Quick recap while it's fresh so we have aligned next steps. High-level notes from our side: 

- Primary pain: inference unit economics are currently the gating factor for your fraud model expansion. You said per-transaction inference cost is ~2.5–3x target.
- Current stack: models run on AWS SageMaker multi-instance endpoints (g4dn fleet), fp16; no centralized prefix/KV cache today.
- Performance expectation: success criteria you shared: p95 tail for approval flow <180ms, and monthly inference spend reduction ~40% (first 90 days).
- Openness to techniques: team is open to batching and caching tradeoffs; conservative on quantization — willing to evaluate 4-bit if we can guarantee equivalent decision accuracy on the fraud classifier.

What we (Redwood) will bring:
- A simple cost model showing projected per-100k transaction token costs across batching, KV caching, and a quantized variant.
- A proposal for a 4–6 week pilot (10k DAU simulated, can run as shadow traffic) with measurable gates for latency and top-line cost reduction.
- A short tech deep-dive to the SRE/infra team to align on networking, logging, keys (KMS) and any VPN/VPC considerations.

Agreed next steps: 
1) I’ll share a draft cost model & MAP (attached) by EOD Monday.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your SREs (Ravi, can you share 2x 60-min slots this week?).
3) We’ll scope pilot acceptance criteria (latency SLOs, quality checks, rollback plan).

Questions for you (quick):
- Can you confirm the current typical request size (avg tokens in prompt + instructions)? Ballpark is fine.
- Do you have any hard constraints on model families (e.g., cannot use community models)?

Thanks — appreciate the openness. If anything above is off, tell me and I’ll correct.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0187

Attachment: helixpay-cost-model-v1.xlsx (XLSX, 42KB)

From: Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@helixpay.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: HelixPay SRE <sre@helixpay.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HelixPay discovery — cost sensitivity & next-step checklist

Thanks Jasmine — very useful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Average prompt size: roughly 320 tokens (including system instruction and metadata). Some high-risk flows spike to ~1,200 tokens.
- Model policy: we prefer to stay on models with commercial licenses (no "research-only" restrictions). Open to community models if they have a permissive license and Redwood verifies performance.
- SRE availability: I can do Wed 12:00–13:00 PT or Thu 09:00–10:00 PT for the deep-dive. Thu is preferred.

We are definitely cost-sensitive — the product team has a cap on infra that will drive whether we scale this feature. Happy to review the cost model and pilot plan.

Also tagging in our SRE lead — cc'd — to confirm networking constraints.

Regards,
Ravi
Head of Data Platforms
HelixPay
ravi.menon@helixpay.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@helixpay.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: HelixPay discovery — cost sensitivity & next-step checklist

+1 on Thu 09:00 PT for the deep-dive. I started a quick pass on the cost model assumptions — we should validate: tokenization mismatch (your token counts are likely measured earlier in the pipeline), model seq len headroom, and whether they have a hard limit on batch-induced 95th latency. I’ll add a separate tab in the MAP for batching sensitivity.

Proposed pilot gates (draft):
- Gate 1 (safety): no >0.5% regression in classifier precision/recall on hedged dataset.
- Gate 2 (latency): p95 < 180ms with throttling strategy for burst windows.
- Gate 3 (cost): projected -35% (conservative) to -45% (optimistic) per-transaction inference cost.

Sharing the draft spreadsheet now (Jasmine: please attach).

— Aditya
Principal Solutions Eng, Redwood
aditya.rao@redwood.com

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@helixpay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, HelixPay SRE <sre@helixpay.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HelixPay discovery — cost sensitivity & next-step checklist

Great — thanks for the quick replies and the slots. I’ve attached two files: the MAP (helixpay-cost-model-v1.xlsx) with batching/caching scenarios and a short note on quantization tradeoffs (redwood-quantization-tradeoffs.pdf). Ravi — I penciled the deep-dive for Thu 09:00 PT and sent a calendar invite to everyone cc'd.

Immediate asks for your SRE ahead of Thu:
- Confirm whether HelixPay can accept outbound connections to our pilot endpoints (we can also run in your VPC if needed).
- Share any egress/NAT throughput constraints and IP allowlist process.
- List any KMS/HSM controls required for keys (we support customer-managed KMS).

Next actions (owner / ETA):
- Jasmine: finalize pilot MOP & MAP (attached) — EOD Mon (done).
- Aditya: scope batching sensitivity tab & pilot acceptance gates — Wed EOD.
- Ravi: confirm Thu slot and share any networking redlines — Tue EOD.

I’ll follow up post deep-dive with a scoped statement of work and a proposed pilot timeline. Looking forward to it.

Best,
Jasmine

Attachments: helixpay-cost-model-v1.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB); redwood-quantization-tradeoffs.pdf (PDF, 110KB)
